apps/web/src/components/two-step-sign-in.tsx (Account and preferences), sign-in code step in auth-form.tsx
Organisation rule: GET/PUT /v1/orgs/:orgId/security (org_security_settings); AuthGuard refuses MFA_REQUIRED; apps/web/e2e/two-step-required-flow.test.mjs
SEC-005.notes: Authenticator-app codes (TOTP) and ten single-use recovery codes; an organisation can require it for every member. SMS and email codes are not offered.

evidence: /v1/orgs/:orgId/expense-allowance-rates; claim lines with allowance { rateId, quantity, from, to, purpose }
EXP-006.notes: Mileage at organisation rates per km (vehicle types as named rates). No map/GPS distance lookup.

evidence: /v1/orgs/:orgId/expense-allowance-rates; claim lines with allowance { rateId, quantity, from, to, purpose }
EXP-008.notes: Per diem at organisation daily rates (places as named rates), whole or half days.

EXP-013.notes: Limits per receipt, day, month (per claimant, across live claims) and claim; by category or for everything.

EXP-015.notes: Blocking rules stop submission and approval; warnings need the approver's reason.

EXP-022.notes: Rule-based detection covers limits, missing receipts, receipt age and possible duplicates. Statistical anomaly checks are shown for a second look and never block: unusual amount (over 3 times the 12-month category median with robust z above 3.5), just under a per-receipt limit, and receipts split around a limit. No machine-learning model is used.

evidence: apps/api/src/reports/reports.service.ts cashMovements; GET reports/income-statement?basis=CASH; export basis=CASH
GL-014.notes: Cash-basis profit and loss derived from the accrual ledger (payments, credits applied, claims paid back, payroll payments, bank entries). Balance sheet stays accrual.

evidence: apps/api/src/banking/banking.service.ts transferSuggestions/recordTransfer; GET banking/transfers/suggestions, POST banking/transfers
BANK-007.notes: Same amount out/in across own accounts within 3 days; recorded as one entry matched to both statement lines. Same-currency accounts.

TAX-024.notes: Notice register with deadlines, files, history and outcomes. Not yet in the compliance calendar; no reminders.

evidence: apps/web/src/app/orgs/[orgId]/financial-tags, journal form tag pickers, profit-by-dimension tag tabs
GL-031.notes: Organisation-defined tags with values on journal lines and profit by tag. Not yet on invoice and bill lines, budgets or report export.

evidence: apps/web/src/app/orgs/[orgId]/financial-tags, journal form tag pickers, profit-by-dimension tag tabs
GL-028.notes: Locations as the Location preset of financial tags: values per office, store or branch, picked on journal lines, profit by location. Not yet on invoice and bill lines.

evidence: apps/web/src/app/orgs/[orgId]/purchases/bill-checks, bill page Unusual bill checks card
AP-031.notes: Rule-based checks against the vendor's earlier bills and bank details, with reviews. Fixed thresholds; no AI explanation yet.

GL-023.notes: Receivables and payables subsidiary ledgers (open items per customer and vendor, ageing, statements) with the control account compared to them at any date on Account reconciliations; the open items can be added as the supporting balance.

GL-025.notes: Profit centres are a financial tag (preset Profit centre, key profit_center): values are defined per organisation, journal lines are checked against them, and Profit by tag gives the profit for each centre. Not built: a hierarchy of profit centres.

GL-027.notes: Business units are a financial tag (preset Business unit, key business_unit) with values per organisation, checked on journal lines and reported by in Profit by tag. Not built: separate ledgers or balance sheets per business unit.

GL-033.notes: Same as ENT-008 and ENT-009: intercompany charges and settlements posted in both companies together, reversed together and eliminated on consolidation.

TRS-012.notes: Fixed deposits: placing, interest to date and at maturity, accruals, closing at maturity or early with tax deducted, and reversal. Not built: mutual funds, bonds and shares, market values and gains.

DS-003.notes: Ctrl+K or ⌘K (or Search in the header) opens a search of the pages this person can open and, with reports access, records: contacts, invoices and bills, payments, journals, accounts, projects, departments, loans, fixed assets and alerts. Arrow keys and Enter, or click. No actions (create, run) from the palette yet.

SUBS-024.notes: Percentage or fixed-amount coupons, limited by plan, billing, number of organisations and a use-by date, for the first 1-36 payments or every payment. Taken off before GST at checkout and on renewals while payments are left; shown on the tax invoice; usage and money taken off in Platform admin → Coupons. A coupon never takes a payment to nothing.

SUBS-025.notes: Promotions are coupons applied automatically: shown beside the plans they fit with their last day, and the one taking the most off is applied at checkout without a code for organisations that have not used it. Never stacked with a coupon; not applied to runner-issued renewals.

SUBS-017.notes: Payroll, foreign currencies and group consolidation can be added to a plan that lacks them, priced per currency and billing by platform administrators. Added at checkout (an upgrade for the days left mid-period), removed at the renewal, carried on renewal invoices, listed on the tax invoice, and counted for module access. The AI assistant is not an add-on (its use is set by a plan's AI requests).

GL-034.notes: Consolidation adjustments in the group's currency, in the consolidation only: goodwill, fair value or unrealised profit entered by hand, shown in the worksheet's Adjustments column, voided once with a reason.

GL-036.notes: Rule-based suggestions for a month: manual journals repeated in each of the last three months but missing, and expense accruals at the three-month average. Accepted as draft journals or dismissed with a reason; decisions recorded once and audited.

SEC-038.notes: Platform-wide AI emergency shutdown by a platform super admin with a reason: every agent's guard refuses (503 AI_SHUTDOWN) before any model call, also mid-run; organisations see the reason and cannot lift it; append-only history, audited. The organisation-level stop is AGENT-060.

SEC-030.notes: Every copilot tool needs a permission checked on every call; owners and admins can turn tools off per organisation. A tool that is off or outside the member's role is never offered to the model and is refused if the model calls it anyway; the list is re-read before each tool round. Copilot actions are re-checked when the member confirms.

SEC-013.notes: Rotation of the key that encrypts stored secrets (integrations, payment gateways, CRM webhooks, two-step sign-in): previous keys keep opening what they sealed, a platform admin re-encrypts everything readable with the current key (audited), unreadable secrets are counted and left for re-entry. Not built: KMS/Vault, JWT signing key rotation, per-organisation keys.

SEC-020.notes: Per-organisation retention periods for working data (copilot conversations, CRM webhook delivery log) with minimums, a daily runner and Apply now, audited; statutory records (books, GST, income tax, payroll, audit trail) are never deleted on a schedule and the page lists India's minimum periods. Not built: retention for uploaded files and email logs, legal hold, export before deletion.

SEC-006.notes: Single sign-on with an organisation's OpenID Connect provider (Entra ID, Google Workspace, Okta, Keycloak, ...): code flow with PKCE and browser-bound state, ID token signature/iss/aud/exp/nonce checks, DNS-TXT-verified email domains, optional join with a role and optional enforcement (owners keep their password), audited. Not built: SAML, SCIM, single logout.

SEC-007.notes: OIDC relying party architecture: per-organisation connection with sealed client secret (key rotation covers it), discovery with issuer check, SSRF-guarded provider requests (public https only, no redirects, size and time limits), JWKS verification of RS/PS/ES algorithms. SAML is not supported.

SEC-018.notes: Uploads (attachments, tax notice files, vendor portal) are limited to 5 MB, typed from their bytes (PDF/PNG/JPEG/WebP), renamed safely, refused when a PDF can run code or carries files (also escaped or in compressed object streams), recorded in file_scans and served back as downloads with nosniff and a sandbox CSP.

SEC-019.notes: ClamAV (clamd INSTREAM over TCP, CLAMAV_URL) scans every upload before it is kept; infected files are refused, and uploads fail closed while the scanner cannot answer. Refusals are audited (file.refused) and shown in Platform admin -> File scanning. Not built: re-scanning stored files.

SEC-029.notes: Copilot only. Successful tool results are checked against five patterns (ignore instructions, new role, imitated chat messages, tool requests, requests for hidden prompts or secrets). A match is sent to the model wrapped in a safety notice and <untrusted_data>, recorded on the answer and in the audit, and propose_* tools are refused for the rest of that answer. Pattern-based: rephrased instructions can get through, which is why proposals still need a member's confirmation.

SEC-031.notes: Copilot only. Before a question or tool result goes to the model: Luhn-valid card numbers, Verhoeff-valid Aadhaar numbers and API keys are always replaced; bank account fields (on by default), PAN, emails and phones as owners and admins choose. Members keep the real text; each answer records and shows counts of what was hidden. Other AI agents (collections, bank, close, CFO) do not redact yet.

SEC-034.notes: Two layers checked before every model call by every agent (the shared AI guard): models allowed across Talk2Tax (super admins, with a reason, insert-only history, audited) and an organisation's narrower list (owners and admins, audited). A model not allowed is refused with 409 MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED before anything is sent; it cannot be saved in Settings → Integrations or used by the connection test. Not per agent or per member.

SEC-037.notes: Each agent may start a limited number of AI tasks in any 60 minutes per organisation: its own limit (owners and admins, 1 to 100,000, audited) or the server's AI_AGENT_TASKS_PER_HOUR (default 500, 0 = none). New work over the limit is refused with 429 AI_TASK_LIMIT before anything is sent; running work stops before its next model call only once over the limit. Alongside existing per-run limits (copilot tool rounds and turn timeout), monthly token budgets and the per-member hourly question limit.

SEC-023.notes: Reads the audit trail every SECURITY_MONITOR_INTERVAL_SECONDS (default 5 min). 23 audit actions are security events (HIGH or MEDIUM). Six rules raise alerts: many lockouts in an hour (SECURITY_LOCKOUT_ALERT_COUNT), failed two-step codes after a right password, platform role changes, a platform admin turning two-step off, infected uploads, 5+ SSO refusals in an hour for an organisation. One alert per rule and key (security_alerts; findings never change or get deleted), each new one emailed once to every super admin through the server's mail server. Platform admins review events and alerts; super admins acknowledge with a note (audited). No SIEM export, no pager or chat notifications, no anomaly detection beyond these rules.

BANK-020.notes: Per active bank account, unmatched statement lines and entries grouped into explained exceptions with a suggested action: amounts that differ by up to 2% within 7 days, splits (one item = 2-3 on the other side), reversals (in and out within 7 days), bank charges or interest by narration, not in the books, in transit (within 7 days of the latest statement line), stale (over 30 days before it) and outstanding; ageing buckets. Deterministic; read-only; statements only (no live bank feed).

EXP-023.notes: Unusual expenses page and the Unusual expense claims alert check: claims submitted in a period with serious or medium warning signs (duplicate receipts across claims, splits around a limit, unusually large, just under a limit, repeatedly just under, old receipts, missing receipts) raise critical or warning alerts that clear when the claim is rejected or voided. Deterministic; no AI model.

EXP-024.notes: Fraud risk indicators on expense claims across claims and people: the same receipt (date, amount, merchant or category) on another claim, receipts split around a per-receipt limit, someone with 3+ lines just under a limit in 90 days, receipts over 60 days old, receipts of 5,000+ with no file, Sundays and round amounts; a per-claim score (3/2/1 by level) and a People to look at ranking. Signs for review, not proof; deterministic; read-only.

BANK-022.notes: Each bank account's balance week by week for 30/60/90 days from its imported statements: movements that repeat (same narration and direction, 3+, weekly/monthly/quarterly, within 25% of the median) projected from when last seen, the average week of the other movements of the last 13 weeks with a 25th-75th percentile range, starting from the book balance; lowest week-end balance. Deterministic; statements only (no live bank feed).

AP-034.notes: A suggested payment date for each open bill over 30/60/90 days from the bank balances and the predicted customer receipts (AR-033), keeping a chosen balance every day: overdue first, then by due date and priority score (AP-030); a bill waits for receipts when paying it on time would breach the balance, or is shown as not covered. Unverified vendors and bills in batches are listed, not dated. Dates can be applied as AP-007 payment plans (audited). Deterministic; open invoices are the only receipts forecast.

AP-035.notes: Draft bills held by purchase-order match exceptions (AP-017), each difference investigated against the order, goods received and the vendor's bills of the last year: goods not received yet vs billed beyond delivery, likely duplicate (same order line, quantity and price, or same vendor invoice number) vs over-billing, vendor price rise seen on posted bills since the order vs price error, unlinked line, extra charge, closed order. Next step, amount at stake, and accepting confirmed differences from the page. Rule-based and explained; no AI model.

EXP-016.notes: As of any date: the Employee Reimbursements Payable balance against approved claims not yet reimbursed or voided, with every difference itemised (entries no claim made, claims whose own entries differ); claims owed by employee and age (over 30 days overdue); reimbursements of the last 90 days against imported bank statements (matched, not on the statement once statements run 3+ days past, or awaiting the statement). Read-only and deterministic.

AR-037.notes: The likely reason for an invoice dispute (price, quantity, quality, not received, billed twice, tax, other) from the customer's words (scored phrases and words) and the invoice (another invoice for the same total within 45 days; disputed amount equal to the tax), with confidence and what it is based on. Suggested live while raising or changing a dispute, one click to apply; recorded disputes whose reason looks wrong are flagged. Rule-based and explained; no AI model.

EXP-020.notes: Receipt lines on expense claims suggest the likely expense account while typing: the same merchant on approved and reimbursed claims of the last two years (share of its lines per account), kinds of spending named in the merchant or description (taxi, hotel, restaurant, phone, software...) matched to account names, and description words seen on earlier lines. Up to three accounts with HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW confidence and reasons; nothing is booked until the person presses Use. Rule-based, no AI model.

AP-020.notes: Bill lines suggest the expense account from the vendor's posted bills of the last two years, the kind of spending named in the description and words seen on earlier bill lines, with confidence and reasons; the person presses Use. Same rules as EXP-020. Only expense accounts are suggested (not inventory or asset lines).

AP-026.notes: Code lines from history on a new bill: each line's expense account (same rules as AP-020), then the tax rate, department and project that more than half of the vendor's earlier posted lines on that account had (active ones only), with reasons. Fills blank fields only; the person reviews and saves. Deterministic, no AI model call; document extraction (AP-025) is separate.

AP-036.notes: The copilot can list bills to pay and propose a draft supplier payment batch (sensitive, confirmed twice by the member). Confirming only prepares a draft as that member; it is always approved by someone other than the member who accepted it, even where self-approval is otherwise allowed. Approving, the bank file, recording payments, transfers and bank-detail changes can never be assistant actions (startup check and database kind check). Positive and negative cases tested in API and browser.

AR-043.notes: Every email passes the policy in MailerService.send: never to a contact who opted out (append-only consent history with reason, audited), AI-drafted messages only after a person approves, and an owner can stop automations emailing customers and vendors. Collections skip opted-out customers and re-check at send (409 OPTED_OUT, audited communication.blocked); automation emails to contacts fail with the reason. Positive and negative tests against real SMTP. Not built: self-service unsubscribe links, SMS/WhatsApp consent, quiet hours.

AR-041.notes: Hand-made invoices to customers with contracts matched to the contract they most likely bill (lines by account and description, prices, period total, date in term; score 0-100, strong at 80). Shows the period, billing twice, earlier periods unbilled, voided or skipped periods and line-by-line price differences. Count as period N records the invoice as the contract's next period so the runner does not bill it again (locked, re-checked, contract history + audit); dismiss with reason (append-only, audited). Not built: reading terms from contract PDFs, language-model explanations.

EXP-025.notes: Forecast of expense-claim spending by account for 1-6 months from 12 months of approved/reimbursed claim lines (by spend date): last-3-month average, seasonal factor (0.5-2) with 10+ months of history, range from the 6-month spread, trend vs prior 3 months; irregular accounts listed separately; spent so far, owed to employees and waiting approval. Decimal-only, deterministic. Not built: bills/payroll in this view, department budgets, hand-entered planned spend.

EXP-014.notes: Department per expense claim line (validated active DEPARTMENT dimension, carried to the journal debit). Yearly budget per department (budgets.manage, audited, department_budgets collection). Report: spent from ledger expense lines with the department, waiting from submitted claims, left, year-end pace; Over / At risk / On track / No budget, worst first. Approvers see per-department impact on a submitted claim. Never blocks. Not built: monthly or per-account budgets, over-budget alerts.

TAX-045.notes: Monthly GST reconciliation: movement on the six GST accounts vs the month's documents (GSTR-3B basis), GST payments shown apart, every difference explained per journal entry (manual journal, document from/posted in another period, voids, posting differs). Read-only. Not built: GSTR-2A/2B portal matching, quarter/year view.

TAX-044.notes: Discrepancy checks on the month's posted GST documents: wrong tax heads (IGST vs CGST/SGST), unequal CGST/SGST, tax on exempt lines, tax not at the rate (>1.00), invalid GSTIN, supplier GSTIN state mismatch, ITC without supplier GSTIN, missing HSN, one HSN at different rates; severity High/Medium/Low. Deterministic, no AI.

TAX-048.notes: Tax payments due in 1-6 months from the compliance calendar (GSTR-3B/PMT-06, TDS/TCS, PF, ESI, PT, advance tax) incl. overdue: known from the books when the period is over (GST payment preview after set-off as one running balance; undeposited TDS/TCS; unpaid pay-run dues), advance tax from the plan, otherwise 3-period average with 6-period std-dev range; totals by due month. India only, read-only. Not built: interest/late fees, unissued sales, self-assessment tax.

TAX-047.notes: Open compliance-calendar deadlines (GSTR-1/3B, TDS/TCS, PF, ESI, PT) in the next 7-120 days scored HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW from the last 365 days' record (filing dates, deposit/payment dates; missed = late), median lead, days left, and book readiness (GST reconciliation discrepancies/differences for ended months, missing pay runs). Rule-based, read-only, no AI. Not built: advance tax, annual returns.

EXP-019.notes: Receipts for company-paid spending (merchant, date, amount, file as EXPENSE_RECEIPT attachment) matched to money-out bank statement lines: suggestions scored on amount (exact/within 2%), date gap (<=10 days) and merchant words in the narration, one-to-one, ties never Sure; match one, all sure ones, or undo with a reason; bank spending without a receipt (no match or line attachment). Employees see their own receipts. Read-only on the books; no AI. Not built: OCR, card feeds, email-in receipts.

TAX-026.notes: Form 3CD working papers for a financial year (India): 44AB(a) applicability with the 5% cash test, 40A(3) cash payments over 10,000 per person per day, 269ST cash receipts of 2 lakh or more, TDS late deposits with 201(1A) interest from the TDS register, clause 44 spending by supplier GST registration. Read-only, no AI. Not built: transporter limit/rule 6DD, 43B, 269SS/T, composition split, filing.

TAX-025.notes: Compliance document records (acknowledgement, challan, return copy, working, registration, notice, other) linked to compliance-calendar obligations from the last year/next 30 days, files as COMPLIANCE_DOCUMENT attachments, keep-until date (end of 8th FY after the period; registrations while registered), void with reason (never deleted), and a missing-documents list: filed returns without acknowledgement and made payments without challan (with a file). India only. Not built: portal download, older periods, retention reminders.

AP-033.notes: Deterministic negotiation brief per vendor billed in the last 12 months: price rises (>=5%, saving = paid above first price), same HSN/description cheaper from another vendor (>=3%, saving on quantity bought), volume (+20% or 25% share), good payment record (ask +15 days or early-payment discount), C/D scorecard grade, caution when paying late or overdue. Read-only. Not built: AI-drafted negotiation emails, outside market prices.

EXP-026.notes: Approved claims grouped per person and routed: bank transfer when the employee record (matched by email) has a salary account, cash otherwise, wait for cash when no account has room after the amount kept, needs bank details when there is no cash account. Overdue (>7 days since approval) first; last-used account preferred while it has room. Pay the ready ones in one step through the usual reimbursement journal. Not built: payment files for bank transfers, adding reimbursements to payroll.

EXP-027.notes: Evidence per decided claim collected from the records: receipt files with SHA-256, approver and time, policy exceptions with the approver's note (from the audit trail), posted journal, reimbursement, bank statement match (gap once the statement runs 3+ days past the payment; cash n/a), hash-chained audit events. Gaps-only filter, evidence pack per claim, CSV evidence index with formula guard. Not built: zipped pack of the files themselves.

AP-032.notes: Vendor contracts (vendor_contracts collection: term, payment terms, spend cap, items-only, price list by HSN/description; fixed terms, terminate with reason, audited). Posted bills checked against the contract covering their date: price above contract (excess x qty), over the spend cap, shorter payment terms, after the term with no other contract, item not on the list. Read-only checks. Not built: contract PDF extraction, blocking bills at entry.

TAX-049.notes: What-if scenarios against the advance tax estimate: change in sales and deductible expenses (with GST rates), extra depreciation, non-deductible add-backs and regime switch; gives taxable income, corporate tax with surcharge/marginal relief/cess, change vs estimate, net payable after credits, profit after tax, effective rate, net GST on the change and cash effect. Regimes compared on the estimate. Saved scenarios (tax_scenarios) recomputed on every read, audited. Not modelled: loss carry-forward, MAT, instalment timing; India only.

RPT-009.notes: Tax report for a period (FY to date by default, up to 2 years): output/input tax by rate and month from posted invoices, credit notes, bills and vendor credits (FX converted, GST heads), reverse charge, TDS/TCS by section, and every tax payable/receivable/expense account with opening, debits, credits and closing from the ledger. CSV export with formula guard, audited. Read-only.

RPT-010.notes: Payroll report over a range of months (FY to date by default, up to 24): totals from posted payslips, statutory amounts (PF employee/employer incl. EDLI and admin, ESI, PT, TDS), by month with gross change flagged at 10%, by employee, draft runs listed. CSV export audited. No bank details. Read-only.

RPT-021.notes: Audit report over a period of days (FY to date by default, up to two years, org time zone) from the hash-chained audit trail and posted journals: activity by person and record type, sensitive actions in 7 categories (periods reopened, access, bank details, deletions, voids/reversals, settings, exports), journal checks (posted >30 days late, round manual >=100000 in multiples of 10000, self-posted manual), chain verified. CSV export audited. Read-only.

RPT-022.notes: Executive report per fiscal quarter or year: headline (revenue growth on prior period and last year, gross/net margin, cash, runway), summary P&L vs prior period and last year, months, named top customers, points for attention (net loss, revenue -10%, margin -5 pts, runway <12 months, customer >=30%), narrative. Live while draft; finalising after period end freezes figures and narrative, later postings listed. Audited.

RPT-023.notes: Investor report per fiscal quarter or year: same headline, P&L comparison and months as the executive report, revenue concentration without customer names, no internal attention points, investor update (highlights, challenges, outlook, asks). Separate from the executive report; finalise freezes; audited.

EXP-007.notes: Business trips: request with purpose, destination, dates and a four-part estimate; approve/reject by someone other than the traveller; traveller links own non-void claims (one trip per claim) and unlinks until approved; cost against the estimate (spent, pending, by category, per day, over-estimate and lines outside the dates). Mileage and per diem come in through claims (EXP-006/008). No booking integration or travel advances.

TAX-019.notes: Computation of total income for a financial year (India): book profit before tax excluding income tax expense, add back book depreciation, deduct section 32 depreciation entered by the preparer, 40A(3) cash payments from the tax audit working, preparer adjustments with sections, brought forward business loss set-off and carry forward; tax on income rounded under 288A, credits from the advance tax plan's TDS and advance tax accounts; saved per year, finalised (immutable) with later-posting note. Not built: MAT, other heads, Chapter VI-A, 234A-C interest, ITR filing.

TAX-020.notes: Corporate tax on the computation: 22% (115BAA), 25% (turnover up to 400 crore), 30% companies and firms with surcharge, marginal relief and 4% cess, less TDS, advance tax and other tax paid, giving self-assessment tax or refund. Not built: MAT (115JB), dividend/buyback tax, 234A-C interest.

TAX-051.notes: Tax audit readiness for a financial year (India), from the books: months locked, year closed, no drafts, banks reconciled to year end, returns/payments for the year done and on time, acknowledgements/challans on file, 40A(3) cash payments, 269ST cash receipts, TDS late, depreciation posted, income tax computation final. Notes to the auditor per check; mark ready only when nothing missing and attention points explained (snapshot, frozen notes, changed-since list); reopen with reason; CSV checklist export. No AI. Not built: auditor portal sharing, auditor sign-off, filing.

TAX-003.notes: Tax rates are effective-dated and version-controlled: original rate = version 1, later versions with effective date, reason and who (tax_rate_versions, append-only). Documents use the rate in force on their issue date (incl. GST split), expense claim lines on the line date; list shows rate today and next change. Versions only in date order, never behind posted documents/approved claims; scheduled versions withdrawable with reason before they take effect. Audited. Not built: central rate publishing, dated withholding section versions beyond validFrom, date-aware line-editor previews.

TAX-050.notes: Each tax notice is analysed from its authority and section/form against a source-cited table (GST s.46/61/73/74/74A, IT 139(9)/143(1)(a)/142(1)/143(2)/148A/148/156/245, TDS 200A): type, what it asks, usual reply period, deadline (entered date wins, else from receipt with a warning), how to reply, checklist with saved ticks, interest at 1% per month or part under s.220(2) on an unpaid IT demand, related notices for the same period. Unknown sections are not guessed; the user can choose the type. Audited. Not built: reading notice PDFs, GST s.50 interest and penalties, Income-tax Act 2025 section numbers.

TAX-032.notes: Builds on reverse-charge bills: Tax -> Reverse charge shows the month's register of RCM bills and vendor credits with tax by head (to pay in cash), notified categories matched by HSN/SAC with source (Notifications 13/2017 and 4/2017-CT(Rate)), posted bills that may have missed reverse charge, and self-invoices for unregistered/foreign suppliers (s.31(3)(f), due in 30 days under rule 47A) numbered RCM/FY/seq, one per bill, immutable, audited. Not built: payment voucher (s.31(3)(g)), foreign-currency RCM, s.9(4) promoters, suggestion while entering a bill.

TAX-052.notes: Each invoice, credit note, bill and vendor credit with tax explains how its tax was worked out (place of supply, intra/inter-state, export, reverse charge, input tax credit, notes, foreign currency, each line's tax and rate version, TDS/TCS) with every point citing its source: a record in the books or the provision of law (IGST/CGST Acts, CGST Rules, rate notifications, Income-tax Act 2025 s.393). Things to check are flagged. Built from the posted figures and fixed rules; no AI model. Not built: Hindi text, journals/claims/payroll, links to provision text.

BANK-004.notes: Token-authenticated feed per bank account: a sender posts JSON transactions (deduplicated by its own id) or OFX/QIF/MT940 files (deduplicated like uploads). Deliveries are recorded with reasons for refusals; lines on or before the last reconciliation are refused; health shows late or failing feeds. No built-in connection to a particular bank or aggregator.

TAX-030.notes: UK nine-box VAT return on the invoice basis from posted invoices, credit notes, bills, vendor credits and approved expense claims; voids taken off in the void period; VRN modulus 97 check; monthly or quarterly staggers with due dates; per-rate VAT treatments (standard/reduced/zero/exempt/outside scope); other entries on the VAT accounts listed; submissions recorded (vat_returns, immutable); later changes to submitted periods carried as corrections within HMRC's £10,000 / 1% of box 6 up to £50,000 limit. Not submitted to HMRC (no MTD connection); no cash/flat-rate/margin schemes, domestic reverse charge, PIVA, partial exemption or NI EU trade.

TAX-036.notes: Singapore GST F5 boxes 1-8 and 13 (revenue from the ledger) from posted invoices, credit notes, bills, vendor credits and approved expense claims; standard/zero/exempt/out-of-scope treatments (no reduced rate; 7/8/9% standard), UEN/M-number format check, monthly or quarterly periods due one month after the end, submissions recorded, back-dated errors up to S$1,500 net GST carried to the next return (above: GST F7). Not filed with IRAS; boxes 9-12 and 14+ (import schemes, tourist refunds, bad debt relief, pre-registration claims, reverse charge), blocked input tax and partial exemption not modelled.

TAX-041.notes: Jurisdictions are added one at a time behind a common VAT/GST return layer (registration number, treatments, periods, due dates, boxes, correction limits): United Kingdom (TAX-030), Singapore (TAX-036), Australia (TAX-035), Canada (TAX-034), the UAE (TAX-033) and Germany (TAX-031) so far, each with its own return cycles, card titles and correction window, India with its own GST engine. Other countries stay at starter or accounting-only level until their module is built and tested.

TAX-035.notes: Australian BAS GST items (Simpler BAS) G1, 1A and 1B in whole dollars on the accruals basis from posted invoices, credit notes, bills, vendor credits and approved expense claims; taxable/GST-free/input-taxed/out-of-scope treatments (no reduced rate), ABN check digits, monthly or quarterly BAS with ATO due dates (21st; 28th, December quarter 28 February), lodgments recorded, back-dated errors up to A$10,000 within 18 months carried to the next BAS (above: revise the earlier BAS). Not lodged with the ATO; G2-G20, cash basis, PAYG, fuel tax credits, WET/LCT and tax-invoice checks not modelled.

TAX-034.notes: Canadian GST/HST return (regular method) lines 101 and 103-109 from posted invoices, credit notes, bills, vendor credits and approved expense claims, line 101 from ledger revenue in whole dollars; GST 5% and HST 13/14/15% taxable, zero-rated, exempt, out of scope; business number Luhn + RT account check; monthly or quarterly periods due one month after; filings recorded; input tax credits missed earlier claimed on the next return within four years, other changes sent back to the earlier return. Starter HST rates added. Not filed with the CRA; PST/QST, place of supply, Quick Method, line 104/107 adjustments, instalments and the annual period not modelled.

TAX-033.notes: UAE VAT 201 (first GCC country): boxes 1a-1g by emirate (all supplies in the business's own emirate, chosen at registration), 4, 5, 8, 9, 11-14 from posted invoices, credit notes, bills, vendor credits and approved expense claims; standard 5%/zero/exempt/out-of-scope treatments, TRN format check, monthly or quarterly periods due 28 days after, submissions recorded, errors up to AED 10,000 carried to the next return (above: voluntary disclosure, Form 211). Not submitted to the FTA; tourist refunds, reverse charge, imports, profit margin scheme, partial exemption and blocked input VAT not modelled. Saudi Arabia, Bahrain and Oman returns not prepared yet.

TAX-031.notes: EU VAT starting with Germany: the Umsatzsteuer-Voranmeldung Kennzahlen 81 and 86 (whole-euro bases with the tax worked out at 19% and 7%), 43, 48, 66 and 83 from posted invoices, credit notes, bills, vendor credits and approved expense claims on the accruals basis; standard/reduced/tax-free with and without input tax deduction/not taxable treatments, USt-IdNr. check digit, monthly or quarterly periods due on the 10th, submissions recorded, changes to filed periods flagged for a corrected return (never carried). Not sent through ELSTER; intra-EU trade, reverse charge, § 19, cash accounting, permanent extension, annual return, OSS and ZM not modelled. Other member states not prepared yet.

RPT-026.notes: Arrange mode on a dashboard: drag approved metrics into gaps (new figure) or onto figures, charts and tables, drag widgets to reorder, remove; each drop saved as a new version for the whole organisation, checked by the engine (charts never mix units), audited. Keyboard alternative: pick a metric and Add here / Add to this widget, Move earlier/later buttons.

AP-025.notes: Bill reader: text read from the supplier's PDF (Flate, object streams, ToUnicode fonts, positioned text) or pasted text; deterministic parser finds supplier (by GSTIN or name), bill number, dates, currency, items (qty x rate = amount, HSN), taxes, rounding and total, with field sources and checks in words; suggests accounts and tax rate; reviewed in the bill form, saved with the PDF attached and the person's corrections audited. Scans and photos are refused in words (OCR / AI image reading not built).

EXP-011.notes: Provider-agnostic corporate cards: card programmes (one provider, one liability account, t2tc_ token shown once, hash only), corporate cards added by last four digits with holder and monthly limit, freeze/unfreeze/cancel controls the provider reads from the card feed, transactions sent with the token (idempotent by id, settled replaces authorised, refusals with reasons), cardholders explain spending, finance posts it (Dr expense, Cr card account) or excludes it, and spending also on an expense claim by the same person (same amount, within 3 days) is flagged. Full card numbers never reach Talk2Tax. A real provider connection needs that provider's credentials and an adapter calling the card feed.

EXP-012.notes: Virtual cards on the same card programmes: finance asks for a virtual card (holder, purpose, monthly limit, optional supplier); it waits until the provider confirms it through POST /v1/card-feed/cards/:id/issued with its reference, last four digits and expiry, then its spending flows like a corporate card's. A real provider connection needs that provider's credentials and an adapter calling the card feed.

DASH-028.notes: Profit and loss waterfall on Reports → Financial visuals: revenue, cost of sales, gross profit, people, operating costs, depreciation, operating profit, other income, interest and exchange, other expenses, profit before tax, income tax, net profit, from posted journals over a chosen range of months; animated floating bars (no animation under reduced motion) with the same figures in a table.

DASH-029.notes: Sankey of where income goes: revenue accounts flow into income, then to each expense group and its largest accounts and to profit; a loss flows in as a source so both sides balance; accounts running against their nature are named as left out. The flows are also a table.

DASH-030.notes: Spending heatmap: the 12 largest expense accounts by month, cells shaded by amount against the largest cell, each cell a link to that account's general ledger for that month.

DASH-031.notes: Spending treemap by expense group and account, sized by amount with each share of all spending, plus a table of the groups.

DASH-034.notes: Drill-down: choosing a waterfall step, a Sankey group or a spending group lists the accounts behind it with amounts; choosing an account, a Sankey account node, a heatmap cell or a treemap block opens its general ledger for the same months.

DASH-035.notes: Reports → Department performance: revenue, spending, profit and margin per department over a range of months from journal lines booked to departments (closing entries left out), compared as bars, profit month by month as lines and a table, and ranked with share of spending, spending trend (last month against the average before it) and spending in the fiscal year against the EXP-014 department budget (within, near at 85%, over). Unassigned spending is shown apart with its share. Each department opens its own profit and loss for the same months.

DASH-032.notes: Revenue forecast carries an 80% range per month: expected ± the 80th percentile of how far earlier saved forecasts missed at the same months ahead (all errors when fewer than three at that distance; one saved forecast per month counts). With fewer than three judged months the range runs from committed to best case and says so. Drawn as a shaded band on the forecast chart with a 'How sure the forecast is' table.

DASH-033.notes: Reports → Financial timeline: posted entries (closing entries left out) bucketed by day, week or month (best fit or chosen) with cash in and out through cash and bank accounts (own transfers netted out), the cash balance carried from before the range, and compliance deadlines. Zoom with a brush, filter by kind of entry, choose a bar or period to list its entries and deadlines, open the journal. Up to 400 days.

DASH-036.notes: Reports → Risk monitor: alerts, payment fraud checks, expense risk, unusual bank activity, compliance deadline risk and vendor risk read from their own checks, each scored 0–100 (25/10/3 per high/medium/low finding) with an overall score of 60% worst + 40% mean of active areas; level gauge, areas to look at first, top findings and links to act; one reading a day kept in risk_readings for a 90-day trend and change since the last reading. Areas a role cannot read are left out and the reading is not kept.

DASH-037.notes: Reports → Financial dependencies: an interactive network of the business and the parties its money depends on: customers (revenue from posted invoices less credit notes), vendors (posted bills less vendor credits, before tax), cash and bank accounts and loan/card accounts (balances at the end of the range); shares, Herfindahl–Hirschman concentration per group, dependencies to watch by thresholds (and borrowing above cash), keyboard-operable nodes with details, links to the customer/vendor/ledger and the relationship explorer, group toggles and tables.

DASH-044.notes: Reports → Role dashboards → CEO: the headline (revenue, net margin, net cash flow, runway for the last complete month against the month before), revenue by month (13 months, chart and table), cash today and in 90 days with the lowest point (cash-flow forecast), the risk monitor's score and focus areas, the few things needing attention (risk findings, customers to call, cash short for bills, late-risk deadlines) and the largest customers with shares.

DASH-045.notes: Reports → Role dashboards → CFO: margins with 13-month trends and targets, liquidity and leverage, what is owed both ways (open and overdue receivables and payables, to chase, disputed, to pay now, shortfall, early-payment savings), DSO/DPO, and tax expected over the next 3 months by month.

DASH-053.notes: Reports → Role dashboards → Treasury: cash by cash/bank account, headroom at the lowest expected point above the minimum balance, expected cash by week for 90 days with range and money in/out (chart and table), bills in payment-priority order and invoices customers are expected to pay in the next 30 days.

DASH-063.notes: Reports → Role dashboards → Risk officer: overall risk score with its daily trend, risk by area (scores and findings, linking to each area), concentration of customers, vendors, cash accounts and lenders (largest share, HHI, level), single dependencies by severity and the most serious finding per area.

DASH-064.notes: Reports → Role dashboards → Compliance: counts of overdue, due in 7 days and high/medium late-risk filings and payments, the next deadline, every deadline open over 60 days with risk and reasons (deadline predictions), and tax due over the next 3 months by month.

DASH-066.notes: Reports → Role dashboards → Board and investors: revenue, gross profit, net income and closing cash by calendar quarter of the last 12 months with revenue growth (chart and table), financial position KPIs and customer concentration as a band and shares only; the API and page never name customers, vendors or people (checked in API and browser tests).

DASH-067.notes: Every required dashboard is built and tested, each with its own sections, figures and layout from its own sources rather than one dashboard re-titled: twenty-two role dashboards under Reports → Role dashboards (CEO, CFO, treasury, risk officer, compliance, board, receivables, payables, tax and expense managers, accountant, controller, internal auditor, procurement, payroll manager, AI agent administrator, financial analyst, finance director, department manager, external auditor, project finance, organisation admin), the global super admin dashboard on the platform overview (DASH-042), and the vendor and customer dashboards in their portals (DASH-060/061). The API returns a different shape per role and the browser tests check each one's own sections; tabs a member's role cannot open are shown disabled.

DASH-068.notes: Every required dashboard is built and tested, each with its own sections, figures and layout from its own sources rather than one dashboard re-titled: twenty-two role dashboards under Reports → Role dashboards (CEO, CFO, treasury, risk officer, compliance, board, receivables, payables, tax and expense managers, accountant, controller, internal auditor, procurement, payroll manager, AI agent administrator, financial analyst, finance director, department manager, external auditor, project finance, organisation admin), the global super admin dashboard on the platform overview (DASH-042), and the vendor and customer dashboards in their portals (DASH-060/061). The API returns a different shape per role and the browser tests check each one's own sections; tabs a member's role cannot open are shown disabled.

DASH-049.notes: Reports → Role dashboards → Payables: payables by age (not yet due, 1–30, 31–60, 61–90, over 90 days late; chart and table) with DPO, bills in payment-priority order with pay now / on due / blocked / shortfall and early-payment offers, held bills from bill exceptions with the amount at stake and next step, and payment fraud checks with flagged payments.

DASH-050.notes: Reports → Role dashboards → Receivables: receivables by age (chart and table) with DSO and doubtful count, every overdue customer with amount, invoices and days late (linking to the customer), customers to chase first from collection priorities, and expected collections by week for 8 weeks against due dates.

DASH-051.notes: Reports → Role dashboards → Tax manager: tax expected over 3 months by tax and by payment with basis and range, returns and payments open over 60 days with late risk and what the books show before filing, and last month's GST accounts against documents (agrees, difference, mistakes) when a GST registration exists.

DASH-055.notes: Reports → Role dashboards → Expenses (needs expenses.read as well): claims waiting for a decision oldest first with claimant and total, how long the oldest has waited, the riskiest claims of 90 days with their indicators, card/bank spend of 30 days without a receipt, and each department's expense budget against approved and waiting claims.

DASH-047.notes: Reports → Role dashboards → Controller: the last six months and whether each was closed and certified (with who closed it), past months not closed, duties held apart (segregation-of-duties rules with conflicts to review and reviewed, members whose role allows conflicting steps), controls failed or overdue from the internal controls register, open audit findings, and journals waiting for a second person. Needs audit access (VIEWER sees the tab disabled; API 403).

DASH-048.notes: Reports → Role dashboards → Accountant: work waiting (draft journals, draft invoices and bills, journals awaiting approval, bank lines to sort out), unposted journals oldest first with links, journal approvals waiting (and which are yours to decide), bank accounts with reconciliation exceptions and unmatched statement lines and book entries, and the close status of this month and the two before it.

DASH-054.notes: Reports → Role dashboards → Procurement: open purchase orders (issued and draft) with what is still to receive and to bill, late deliveries past their expected date, vendor contracts ending in the next 60 days or breached by bills (overcharges, bills held against orders), and vendors at high or medium risk with the reasons. Needs purchases access.

DASH-056.notes: Reports → Role dashboards → Internal audit: findings at a glance (open, late, by severity), findings to follow up with owners and due dates, audits in progress, audit evidence still outstanding, and controls that failed. Needs audit access (VIEWER sees the tab disabled; API 403).

DASH-052.notes: Reports → Role dashboards → Payroll: whether this month's pay run is started, a draft or posted; people on payroll; the latest pay runs (and anyone a draft run leaves out for lack of a salary); net salaries and PF, ESI, PT and TDS of the latest posted runs not yet paid, with due dates and late ones marked; payroll cost by month for the last 12 months (gross pay and employer cost as bars and a table, a change in gross of 20% or more flagged); statutory contributions split between employees and employer; joiners and leavers. Needs payroll.read; no bank details are shown.

DASH-062.notes: Reports → Role dashboards → AI agents: whether AI is on, off or stopped for the organisation (or for everyone); calls, failures and suggestions waiting this month; each agent's state, calls, failures, tokens against its monthly budget (80% or more shown in amber), cost at the prices set and last use; how often each agent's suggestions were accepted, edited or rejected in the last 90 days; the latest failed AI calls from the AI decision records. Needs audit.read, like AI control.

DASH-065.notes: Reports → Role dashboards → Financial analyst: every key figure grouped as growth, profitability, liquidity, efficiency and cash, against the month before and the same month last year, with a 13-month sparkline; the figures that moved most from the month before and from last year (engine biggestMovements, relative change, improvement by direction); revenue with gross and operating margins month by month for 12 months (chart and table with totals; engine sharePercent); revenue and net income by calendar quarter with growth; the largest customers and the concentration band.

DASH-046.notes: Reports → Role dashboards → Finance director: this fiscal year's approved budget against actual by quarter and year to date (revenue and net income; planned and actual net income as bars and a table, green better than plan, red worse) with the full-year plan; the accounts furthest off plan, worse-than-plan first (engine furthestOffPlan), including spending not in the plan; departments over budget or at risk with counts by status; the last six closes and past months not closed. Says so when no budget is approved yet.

DASH-059.notes: Reports → Role dashboards → Department manager: choose a department (kept in the address as ?department=); its spending this fiscal year, budget left, claims waiting and budget status; spending month by month against an even monthly share of the yearly budget (chart and table); spending by expense account with shares; expense claims waiting for approval with lines charged to it and how much of each is for it. Needs expenses.read; an unknown department is 404.

DASH-057.notes: Reports → Role dashboards → External auditor: each fiscal year with its year-end status, open, locked and closed periods and profit; the trial balance at the end of the last year that ended (balanced, debits and credits); open periods in ended years; auditor portal links in use with the audit, when they end and how much they were used (never the token); evidence asked for and not yet accepted; audit findings still open. Needs audit.read.

DASH-058.notes: Reports → Role dashboards → Project finance: every project's revenue, cost, profit and margin from everything posted, its health (losing money, thin margin under 10%, healthy, cost with no revenue, nothing posted), how far through its start and end dates it is and days left, and its largest cost account; losses first, with a chart and table. The last six months split into project and other revenue and cost, and the revenue and cost posted to no project with its share. Needs reports.read.

DASH-043.notes: Reports → Role dashboards → Organisation admin: members by role and how many sign in without two-step sign-in, owners or admins without it, whether two-step is required, invitations open, expired, accepted and revoked, the newest members, single sign-on set-up and verified domains, the AI and email integrations and their last test, this month's AI requests and uploads against the plan, and a to-do ranked by urgency that links to where each is fixed. No secret, key or token is shown. Needs org.manage (owners and admins).

DASH-042.notes: Platform administration → Overview is the global super admin dashboard (GET /v1/admin/dashboard, platform.read): a to-do ranked by urgency (security alerts, backup problems, late support tickets, server errors, plan requests, organisations at a limit, trials ending, read-only and suspended organisations) linking to each admin page; new organisations and people by month (chart and table); monthly and yearly run-rate by currency from paid active subscriptions of real organisations (annual price as a twelfth a month) and subscriptions by state, plan requests and trials ending; the fullest organisations this month; organisations by country; the most urgent support tickets; errors, security and backups. Organisation metadata and counts only, never an organisation's books.

DASH-060.notes: The vendor portal (private link, no sign-in) opens with a dashboard: what the vendor is owed by how late it is (not yet due, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, over 90 days) as a chart and table, the next payment due to them and what falls due within 30 days, and the last twelve months of bills (less vendor credits) and payments made to them by month, as a chart and table. Only that vendor's posted bills and payments; no bank account numbers or tokens.

DASH-061.notes: The customer portal (private link, no sign-in) opens with a dashboard: what the customer owes by how late it is as a chart and table, the next payment due and what falls due within 30 days, and the last twelve months of invoices (less credit notes) and their payments by month, as a chart and table. Only that customer's posted invoices and receipts. In the currency with the most open, else the business's own.

RPT-001.notes: Reports → Reporting studio (/reports, GET /reports/studio, reports.read): every report in one catalogue grouped by purpose (statements, ledgers, management, dashboards, tax, payroll and expenses, audit, stakeholders, build your own) with the question it answers, its exports (PDF, Excel, CSV), saved views visible to the member and active schedules; reports the member's role cannot open are listed but closed. Word search across name, question and category. Pins per person (report_favourites, PUT/DELETE /reports/studio/favourites/:report). Totals, the latest exports from the audit trail (report, format, who, when) and the designs built in the report designer. Builds on RPT-002..041.

TAX-039.notes: Invoice content rules for India, the UK, Germany, the UAE, Singapore, Australia and Canada with simplified and stepped tiers, each sourced and dated; every sales invoice and credit note is checked for missing details with the fix; invoices print the seller's VAT number and the tax in the books' currency for foreign-currency invoices. Other countries are reported as not covered.

TAX-040.notes: E-invoicing requirements for India (IRN), Germany (receive 2025, issue 2027/2028), the UAE (2026 pilot, 2027 phases), Singapore (InvoiceNow), the UK (announced April 2029), Australia and Canada (not required), with turnover thresholds tested against completed years in the books or a typed figure. Nothing is sent to any network.

TAX-038.notes: Contacts carry an ISO country; the cross-border report groups posted sales and purchases with contacts abroad by country, lists intra-EU supplies by customer VAT ID for the recapitulative statement, flags taxed exports, untaxed imports, missing VAT IDs and foreign documents without a country, and exports CSV with an audit record.

TAX-028.notes: State permits with the rate charged, economic nexus by state against each state's threshold (this year and last), sales tax by state for a filing period and sales to check (untaxed in a registered state, taxed in an unregistered one, rate differs, no state). Customers carry their state. Local rates, use tax, exemption certificates and filing are not modelled; thresholds need adviser review.

TAX-029.notes: Federal: 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC due for a calendar year's vendor payments from W-9 details (last four TIN digits only), with a reason for every vendor, due dates and CSV export. State: the sales tax returns each permit calls for in the year with tax charged per period. Rules written from memory need US tax adviser review; nothing is filed.

TAX-043.notes: TDS certificates (16A), annual tax statements (26AS/AIS), GST challans (PMT-06) and US 1099s read from PDF or text: recognised, explained, every field with its source line, checked against own PAN/GSTIN and the TDS receivable account; reviewed with a note. Deterministic, no AI; explanations need adviser review.

TAX-046.notes: Known law changes per country with effective dates, impact, what Talk2Tax does and the source; open until recorded as dealt with (audited, final). Built-in rule sets with last-checked dates, stale after 180 days. Scheduled tax rate changes. No live monitoring of government sites; list hand-written and needs adviser review.

TAX-054.notes: Copilot instructions forbid rates, thresholds, sections and legal requirements from memory. Every answer is checked: percentages in tax sentences and section/rule/article references must appear in the tool results or question sent to the model, or the organisation's own tax rates; others are stored on the answer, counted in the audit event, and listed under the answer with their sentence. Deterministic text check that errs towards flagging; it cannot judge whether a rate applies.

EXP-004.notes: OCR with Tesseract (English model shipped with the API, no outside service) on JPEG/PNG/WebP photos, PDF text layer otherwise. Reads merchant, date, total, subtotal, GST/VAT/cess lines, GSTIN (checked) and currency, each with a confidence and warnings; fills the receipt-matching form (and attaches the photo) and expense claim lines. Only a file scan and an audit event are stored. English only; no line-item split.

PERF-014.notes: Budgets for API reads, posting and dashboard interactions, each with a percentile, a limit, the benchmark that measures it in CI and the test conditions. The load test and the dashboard benchmark read their limits from the file.

PERF-015.notes: p95 of 5 timed runs after a warm-up, production build, Chromium 1440x900, 120 invoices/40 bills/20 customers: open dashboard, drill down to receivables ageing, back. Measured on the CI runner and one dev machine only (about 0.5-0.6 s against 2 s).

PERF-021.notes: CI fails when a PERF feature with a time target is claimed without a budget, or a budgeted feature is claimed without its benchmark as evidence, or a benchmark does not run in CI or hard-codes its limit.

PERF-006.notes: Eleven background runners in each API process, each with an interval setting (0 = off), reporting every pass to system health (failing, late), paused during maintenance.

PERF-019.notes: Two API processes on one database run the same passes at once: recurring journals, recurring bills, renewals and reminders, security alerts and workflows each act once; transactions leave nothing half done. Fixed: duplicate subscription renewal and reminder, and a failing security scan, when two servers ran together. Emails sent just before a crash may repeat.

PERF-003.notes: 28 people at 3 requests a second on one machine. With 8 people in one organisation, its posting p95 was 706 to 725 ms on the dev container, after postings of one organisation were made to take turns.

PERF-010.notes: Caches the auth guard's per-request lookups only; emptied by this process's writes and a change stream. Reads p95 about a third faster on the dev container; posting unchanged.

PERF-012.notes: Header search walks one index per field (orgId + field), tests the text on index entries and fetches only matching records, at most a page per field; budget search-at-volume-p95 300 ms in the CI volume test.

PERF-013.notes: PDF bills are read in the background: upload answers 202 QUEUED, a worker takes each reading with a lease (once across servers), retries up to 3 times, FAILED with a reason; pages poll until read. Pasted text stays synchronous.

PERF-020.notes: Governance → AI performance: calls, failures and why, median/p95/slowest time, tokens and answers cut short, per assistant and per day over 7/30/90 days, from the AI decision records (figures only, audit.read).

PERF-005.notes: Every AI call goes through per-server lanes: people's calls before background work, background capped below the total, a per-organisation share, waits then 503 AI_BUSY (decision record AiBusyError); System health shows the AI work lanes.

PERF-011.notes: MONGODB_REPLICA_READS=reports sends report pages' reads to a secondary (secondaryPreferred, maxStalenessSeconds 120 by default); guards, transactions, writes and read-cache loads stay on the primary; System health shows members and setting.

PERF-008.notes: Several API servers on one database: RATE_LIMIT_STORE=database shares rate-limit windows (atomic upsert, TTL); api_instances lists running servers in System health with problems for per-server rate limits and mixed versions; DB closes last on shutdown.

PERF-001.notes: Background work stays bounded with thousands of organisations: alert checks rotate through org_rotations (due by index, claimed, at most 200 looked at per pass); scheduled reports read only due schedules in pages (no 5,000 cap); close auto-start pages; every tenant collection has an orgId-first index (checked).

evidence: scripts/volume-test.mjs › complex reports p95 under 1,000 ms (CI step Volume test)
PERF-004.notes: Complex reports (cash flow, statutory with comparatives, cash basis, vendor spend, receivables ledger, KPIs, management and tax reports) timed at volume in CI against complex-reports-at-volume-p95 (1,000 ms); all under 600 ms p95 on 2,000 invoices + 400 bills.

PERF-009.notes: Decision: not sharded yet (one replica set holds ~63,000 busy organisation-years at the 2 TB review size). System health card shows sizes vs PARTITIONING_REVIEW_DATABASE_GB/COLLECTION_GB and readiness to shard by orgId; CI baseline stops new unique indexes that block sharding (193 ready, 57 need orgId prefix, 12 global lookups).

DASH-026.notes: Relationship explorer → Connection map: the chosen record in the centre and its connections around it, one sector per kind of connection, coloured by kind of record; focus or point to read why it is connected, choose to walk to it (keyboard operable); up to 36 drawn, shared out so every kind appears, the rest counted and listed.
